stories.title: China’s view of Trump’s America has changed from alarm to a shrug
stories.summary: There is no shortage of Western commentary on US President Donald Trump’s second term. What’s missing is an honest account of how 1.4 billion of us in China see it – or at least how China’s officials and scholars do, since that’s who I can speak for here. I’ve spent a decade watching that view change, from real alarm in 2017 to something closer to a shrug today. Four things now count as consensus among Chinese scholars. stories.title: Sharing dangerous driving videos is 'truly reprehensible', PM says
stories.summary: The government has urged social media companies to remove posts celebrating dangerous driving, as Prime Minister Andy Burnham branded sharing them "truly reprehensible". Earlier Defence Minister Luke Pollard told BBC Breakfast on Monday that "social media companies could take the content down easily and adjust their algorithms to stop it being distributed. Two police officers died when a car going the wrong way down a dual carriageway crashed into their vehicle near Middlesbrough on Saturday. The five passengers in the other car were also killed. A TikTok account believed to belong to one of the five passengers, 18-year-old Makai Saddington, shared videos appearing to show dangerous driving, which have since been removed. Pollard said the government had "already taken steps" to tell social media companies to take down such content. He added: "They know exactly what content is on their site, they know how their algorithm works. "They also know that people post content to get views and the more views you get, sometimes you get money for it, so it's a financial incentive to post outrageous content that gets more people watching it." Speaking to reporters in Kyiv, Burnham said the people who share footage glorifying dangerous driving are "doing something that's truly reprehensible". A Downing Street spokeswoman said "the glorification of dangerous driving for clips and entertainment is utterly disgraceful". She added that the culture secretary has been clear that footage should be removed by social media platforms "in line with their legal obligations", and that Ofcom has the government's "full backing to take action" against those that fail in their duties. Video content featuring illegal activity is not necessarily illegal itself - according to the Online Safety Act - it is up to the social network to decide whether flagged content is illegal and act accordingly.

stories.title: Russia wins silver in men’s relay at 2026 UIPM Pentathlon World Championships
stories.summary: The gold went to the team from the UK, while Germany took the bronze
article_sentences: BEIJING, August 24.
Russian pentathletes Yegor Gromadsky and Andrey Bobrov won silver on Monday in the men’s relay at the 2026 UIPM Pentathlon World Championships in China.
The gold went to the team of Ross Charlton and Sebastian Forrest from the UK, while Germany’s Marvin Dogue and Moriz Klinkert took the bronze.
Earlier in the day, Russia’s Viktoria Sazonova and Yana Solovyova took the championship’s silver in the women’s relay.
Running in China’s Guiyang on August 23-30, this year's world championships mark Russia's first appearance since 2019.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) announced a decision on July 7 to provisionally lift an earlier-imposed suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee (ROC) and also recommended lifting restrictions on the participation of Russian athletes in all international tournaments.

stories.title: Cambuur fans suffer burns as fireworks set off during Dutch league match
stories.summary: Game resumed despite injuries to home fans, but it would have been abandoned if a player or match official had been hit. Dutch side SC Cambuur has said fans suffered burns, hearing damage and eye injuries after visiting Feyenoord supporters threw fireworks during a league match in Leeuwarden in the Netherlands province of Friesland. The match on Sunday was halted for about 20 minutes in the first half when fans in the away section lit large numbers of red flares and threw fireworks. Some were aimed towards sections of the ground containing Cambuur supporters, while one exploded on the pitch just a few metres from Feyenoord goalkeeper Tjark Ernst. “Our own goalkeeper had a flare fired at him and only just managed to avoid it,” said Feyenoord general manager Robert Eenhoorn, describing the incident as “simply terrible”. Cambuur said in a statement on Monday that five fans were confirmed to have been injured and that the club would work with the authorities to make sure those responsible were caught. “It should be clear that setting off and firing fireworks is completely unacceptable and has no place in a football stadium whatsoever,” the club added. Leeuwarden Mayor Foort van Oosten also condemned the incident and promised an investigation, while the Dutch football association said it would revisit its protocols for incidents of disorder. The game resumed despite the injuries to the supporters, but it would have been abandoned if a player or match official had been hit. “That doesn’t feel right,” Jan Bluyssen, KNVB manager of professional football competition affairs, told Dutch news agency ANP. “We need to examine whether the protocol is still appropriate and how we might want to adjust it.”
